title: Local-first SDK developer loop and sample apps (notes)
content:
Purpose
This note captures a low-friction, local-first developer loop for SDK contributors and SDK consumers building sample apps. Aim: reduce time-to-hello-world to under 10 minutes, and make an in-repo sample app that also serves as an automated smoke test in CI.

Background / motivation
- We have many standalone quickstarts but developers still get blocked on local env, API keys, and model/quantization selection.
- Developers prefer a single clone -> run flow that: sets up env, runs a small server or CLI example, and demonstrates streaming, function calls, and error handling.
- Also want sample apps that are minimal but realistic: prompt templates, caching example, retry/backoff example, and a small metrics emitter.

Target personas
- Product-engineer wanting to evaluate Redwood API in 10 minutes.
- SDK contributor adding a new language binding or fixing an edge-case.
- Solutions engineer preparing a demo for a customer.

Goals
- A canonical local demo app per SDK (python, node, go) in sdk-examples repo.
- Local env script that sets up virtualenv/npm, injects a dev API key, and starts the demo.
- CI smoke test that runs the demo with a test key in an isolated environment and checks minimal outputs.
- Short quickstart doc page that reproduces the local flow verbatim.

Non-goals
- Full production-grade sample apps with complete auth flows. Keep them intentionally tiny.

Success metrics (how we measure)
- Time-to-first-token: median time for a new user to see an API response after clone < 10 minutes.
- CI: demo smoke tests pass on main for 95% of commits.
- Issue reduction: fewer onboarding issues in 30 days after release.

Proposed artifacts
- repo: sdk-examples/local-first/ (subdirs python-node-go)
- demo app features: hello-chat-streaming, simple-embed-search, cache-demo, retry-demo, telemetry-demo
- local start script: scripts/dev-boot.sh (idempotent)
- README quickstart: docs/quickstarts/local-first.md (one-page, copyable commands)
- CI job: smoke/local-quickstarts with timeout 3m per demo

Local dev loop (developer-facing) - minimal flow
1) clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples.git && cd sdk-examples/local-first/python
2) env: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
3) install: pip install -r requirements.txt
4) dev key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_dev_xxx  # suggest use of dev token manager CLI (see linked artifacts)
5) run: ./scripts/run-dev.sh  # starts small FastAPI app and a demo client that makes 3 requests
6) verify: curl http://localhost:8080/health -> OK; curl http://localhost:8080/chat?prompt=hi -> streaming tokens visible

Developer UX notes
- scripts/run-dev.sh should set up temp cache dir and clear on exit.
- If model not available locally, fall back to hosted small model with a prominent log entry.
- Provide an offline mode that uses a canned json response for CI to avoid external flakes.
- Include a --no-network flag for deterministic runs in CI.

SDK maintainer checklist (for each language)
- minimal public API surface for demo uses (create_client, chat_stream, embed, close)
- telemetry hook: sample emits a local metric to stdout and a structured event to a dev telemetry endpoint
- error handling examples: rate limit -> exponential backoff loop, model mismatch -> graceful fallback
- unit + integration tests: demos run in headless mode in CI and assert on outputs

Quickstart doc outline (docs/quickstarts/local-first.md)
- headline: Local-first SDK quickstart - get to streaming in under 10 minutes
- prerequisites: git, python/node/go, optional docker
- copyable commands (exact lines) for each language variant
- what you should see (sample token stream, sample embed vector shape)
- troubleshooting quick fixes with links to known tickets (JIRA-DEX-294)

CI Integration strategy
- Add a job per language that runs demo with --no-network and asserts exit code 0 and checks for expected JSON keys in output. Keep runtime small.
- To test streaming behavior, run the demo in a short-lived docker container and capture stdout.
- Use a matrix to run node/python/go in parallel and cache installed deps.

Telemetry and usage capture (dev-mode)
- Demo apps emit: demo_start, demo_complete, demo_error (structured json to stdout)
- Document telemetry contract in the README so maintainers can see what fields are expected

Maintenance & release notes
- When SDK major changes affect API, update local-first demos in the same PR as the API change.
- Add a changelog entry in sdk-examples/CHANGELOG.md when the demo behavior or required env changes.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we include a tiny docker image for zero-setup demos? pros: consistency; cons: maintenance burden. (TODO: prototype one)
- How do we securely provide short-lived dev API keys to external contributors? (TODO: discuss with security)
- Where to document default model selection and quantization for local runs? (TODO: link to model-catalog page)

Next steps (immediate)
- Proto: Marcus to create python demo skeleton by 2024-11-12 (PR linked above).
- Lina to draft docs/quickstarts/local-first.md and a one-page cheatsheet by 2024-11-14.
- Sync: 30 minute working session on 2024-11-08 to align on flags and --no-network behavior.

Notes to self and rough edges
- Keep sample prompts short and deterministic.
- Use small random seed in demo to show diversity but keep baseline asserts stable.
- Prioritize a simple UX for contributors: a single script that wraps env creation, lint, and run.

Slack refs: #dev-sdk on 2024-10-30 thread about onboarding blockers.

End of notes.
